report.source_text: A punch biopsy of the nodule confirmed lobular panniculitis with an inflammatory cell infiltrate composed of numerous neutrophils, mixed with lymphocytes, eosinophils, histiocytes and occasional multinucleated giant cells (figure 2A). Granulomas were not observed. No features of vasculitis were identified. Gram-positive cocci were present in the dermis and subcutis (figure 2B). No fungal organisms or acid-fast bacilli were seen on Grocott’s methenamine silver or Ziehl-Neelsen stains. Culture from the punch biopsy grew MRSA.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A female in her 20s with relapsed Hodgkin lymphoma on chemotherapy developed fever and bilateral tender indurated subcutaneous nodules. Initial blood cultures were negative, but punch biopsy cultures grew MRSA. Histopathology of the punch biopsy confirmed lobular panniculitis with neutrophilic inflammatory infiltrate and Gram-positive cocci, without granulomas or vasculitis, consistent with infective panniculitis. Negative autoimmune and tuberculosis tests and normal chest radiograph helped exclude other causes. She was treated with doxycycline leading to resolution of fever and nodules.
